card: Adds an invalid transaction test case containing inputs A, A, B to test non-trailing duplicate inputs. The existing duplicate-input test case only had two inputs, meaning the duplicate was always the last element. The author demonstrates this kills a mutant on MutantHub where duplicate input rejection was restricted to the last input.
evidence: Author cites killing a surviving mutant on MutantHub (#4676) where CheckTransaction only failed duplicate inputs if '&txin == &tx.vin.back()'
problem: Existing consensus transaction validation test vectors for duplicate inputs only tested transactions with two inputs, meaning the duplicate input was always the final input. Test coverage would not fail if a regression only enforced uniqueness on trailing inputs.

risk.why: Only adds an invalid transaction test case; no production or consensus code is modified.

summary: Adds an invalid transaction test case featuring duplicate inputs where the duplicate appears before the final input (specifically inputs A, A, B). This exercises the consensus duplicate-input check in CheckTransaction when the duplicate is not at the end of the input vector.
